statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the publicly reachable age-verification surface. Listing, support, and unknown routes all redirected to that gate; identity submission to third-party providers was intentionally not performed.

paths.description: Homepage redirect and mandatory age-verification gate; covers the only publicly reachable primary task, preferences, accessibility, security, performance, and responsive behavior.
Representative listing archetype. /popular was requested, but the server redirected to the same age-verification gate, so the post-verification listing template was not separately exposed.
Representative support/form archetype. /contact/ was requested and redirected to the gate; legal/support links within the gate were inspected.
Failure/recovery path using a deliberately nonexistent URL; it redirected to the gate without retaining not-found context.

findings.summary: The interface is dark in both default and dark-preference conditions rather than adapting to the user’s requested scheme.
findings.evidence: Default and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are effectively identical; the DOM probe detects theme CSS but no usable light presentation on the audited entry state.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose both light and dark tokens with color-scheme and prefers-color-scheme/light-dark(), retaining the current dark palette for users who request it.

findings.summary: Loading placeholders continue pulsing when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reported roughly 80 running pulse animations at 2000ms each under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
findings.suggestedFix: In the reduced-motion media query, disable the pulse keyframes and replace motion with a static loading treatment.

findings.summary: Provider-state changes and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no view-transition rules while the age-provider chooser changes active state abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Use document.startViewTransition() for provider-state changes and opt eligible same-origin navigations into cross-document transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The site chrome has no scroll-state-aware behavior.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll-state/container-query rules or scroll progress treatment on a content catalogue with long underlying pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight sticky-header/progress treatment so long listing pages expose position without scroll listeners.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout fits at 360px, but the CSS probe found no @container/container-type support for reused catalogue, menu, or dialog components.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment on reusable components and move size-specific component changes to @container rules while retaining viewport-level page layout.

findings.summary: AgeVerif and Yoti are mouse-only clickable divs, and many interactive targets are below 44px.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence shows .provider-option divs with cursor-pointer but no role or tabindex; the modal probe also measured multiple links at 14px high and controls at 36px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use button elements for provider choices with aria-expanded/aria-controls, visible :focus-visible styles, and at least 44x44px target areas.

findings.summary: The age gate misses the good LCP threshold on the measured cold load.
findings.evidence: The trace summary measured LCP at 3133.7ms (FCP 1951.28ms), above the 2500ms good threshold, while TBT remained 0ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the gate’s critical HTML/CSS and defer consent/analytics work until after the essential age-choice UI is painted.

findings.summary: A synchronous third-party consent script is parser-inserted before the gate is usable.
findings.evidence: HAR initiator data flags otSDKStub.js as a parser-inserted High-priority script; DOM confirms it is in head without async, defer, or module.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer CookiePro initialization or load a minimal first-party consent shell first, then fetch the full preference center on demand.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript dominates a simple gate load.
findings.evidence: Scripts transfer 303,149 bytes; GTM alone is 154,526 bytes and CookiePro’s banner SDK is 126,321 bytes, far larger than the 11,351-byte first-party app script.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential tags, delay analytics until consent, and lazy-load the full consent preference-center bundle only when opened.

findings.summary: Two age-verification choices are not exposed as controls to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: AgeVerif and Yoti are clickable div.provider-option elements with no role, tabindex, aria-expanded, or button semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace each provider row with a real button and connect it to its panel using aria-expanded and aria-controls.

findings.summary: The document has no h1 and relies on weak, very small focus indicators for several dialog links.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe starts at h2 and contains no h1; dialog focus outlines are 1px and legal links have 14px-high boxes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one page h1 for the gate, preserve logical heading order, and provide a clearly visible 2px-or-stronger :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: Touch targets in the primary dialog are undersized.
findings.evidence: The dialog focus probe measured the language and primary action controls at 36px high and legal links at 14px high, below the recommended 44px target area.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase control min-block-size to 44px and add padding/spacing around inline legal links so targets remain distinct at zoom and on touch.

findings.summary: Image delivery is wasteful and several images lack intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image probe found six oversized images, five without width/height, seven legacy-format assets, and a 500px logo displayed at 64px.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height for every image and provide appropriately sized AVIF/WebP variants or SVG for logos/provider marks.

findings.summary: The public gate lacks social-share metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found valid Organization JSON-LD but no Open Graph properties on the canonical age-verification page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate og:title, og:description, og:url, and an appropriate non-explicit preview image that matches the visible gate.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP settings weaken otherwise solid transport security.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options are present, but CSP permits unsafe-inline styles; OptanonConsent is not Secure and analytics cookies use SameSite=None for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-inline with hashes/nonces or external styles, mark consent cookies Secure, and shorten/restrict analytics cookie scope and lifetime.

findings.summary: Analytics runs before the user can act on the obscured cookie banner.
findings.evidence: The initial HAR contains a Google Analytics page_view and GTM load while the cookie controls are behind the mandatory age dialog; 347,415 of 434,348 transferred bytes are third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Default analytics consent to denied and do not load GTM/GA until the user has made an accessible, informed consent choice.

findings.summary: Permissions-Policy is missing and privacy cookie posture is permissive.
findings.evidence: The headers probe reports no Permissions-Policy; two analytics cookies are SameSite=None and live for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and tighten analytics cookies to the minimum scope, SameSite mode, and lifetime required.

findings.summary: Provider chooser behavior depends on non-semantic div click handlers.
findings.evidence: The two inactive provider rows are custom clickable divs with no keyboard semantics, making the runtime behavior fragile for keyboard and assistive-technology users.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native buttons and declarative expanded-state attributes so interaction survives input mode changes and script failures more predictably.

findings.summary: Unknown routes are silently replaced by the age gate rather than preserving an error/recovery state.
findings.evidence: A request to a deliberately nonexistent path ended at /age-verification with the normal gate and no not-found message or recovery context.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the requested path through verification, then return a real 404 state with useful links and retry/navigation options.

findings.summary: The gate promises verification-only data use while analytics collection starts before consent is reachable.
findings.evidence: Visible copy says data is used only for age verification and identity stays unlinked, yet the initial network capture sends a GA page_view before the cookie banner can be acted on.
findings.suggestedFix: Align the claim with actual behavior: block analytics until explicit consent and state separately what each verification provider and site analytics process.

findings.summary: Small logos and provider marks are served at far larger intrinsic sizes in legacy formats.
findings.evidence: The image probe found the 500px PNG logo displayed at 64px and provider images up to 400px displayed at 20px; seven images use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve right-sized responsive AVIF/WebP or vector assets and include intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Consent and analytics work consumes most of the entry-load transfer before user interaction.
findings.evidence: Fourteen third-party requests transfer 347,415 bytes, including GTM and eleven CookiePro requests, on a page whose core task is three provider choices.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer analytics and the full preference-center payload until consent or explicit opening, and keep only the minimal gate code on the critical path.

findings.summary: Third-party payload is disproportionate to the age gate’s user value.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for about 80% of transferred bytes (347,415 of 434,348), despite no media playing on the gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove redundant consent payloads, and load analytics only after consent.

taskList.title: Block analytics until accessible explicit consent and align the gate’s privacy claims
Replace provider divs with accessible buttons and enlarge all primary targets
Defer third-party consent/analytics code to improve LCP and reduce transfer
Tighten CSP, Permissions-Policy, and cookie attributes/lifetimes
Right-size images and move legacy raster assets to efficient formats
Add component queries, navigation transitions, scroll-state cues, and share metadata
Preserve requested URLs through verification and expose a recoverable 404 state
